title: Museo de La Plata: Möller and Tempère & Peragallo numbered diatom series, Frenguelli acquisition, and continuing type-reference use

principal_upgrade.previous_state: The Museo de La Plata was known to preserve historical Möller and Tempère & Peragallo diatom collections, but the object-level numbering, acquisition route and current scientific use were not closed.
principal_upgrade.new_state: Recent collection research and taxonomic publications show that numbered Tempère & Peragallo second-edition slides survive at LPC and remain scientifically operative, while biographical and 2025 collection-curation evidence identifies Joaquín Frenguelli as the purchaser/acquirer of Tempère & Peragallo reference material and part of Möller's Typenplatten. A 2025 museum-team poster also quantifies the retained J. D. Möller material as 5 arranged preparations plus 117 mixed-diatom preparations.

official_collection_state.institution: Museo de La Plata, Universidad Nacional de La Plata — División Ficología Dr. Sebastián A. Guarrera
official_collection_state.holdings_statement: The Division holds about 17,000 macro- and microalgal samples and explicitly names the Möller and Tempère & Peragallo collections among its significant historical microalgal holdings, dating them to the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

numbered_tempere_peragallo_objects.current_repository: LPC / División Ficología, Museo de La Plata
numbered_tempere_peragallo_objects.scientific_afterlife: Examined in a modern reassessment of Thalassiosira gravida and designated as the epitype slide after comparison with Cleve's original description and figure.
numbered_tempere_peragallo_objects.evidence_source: Sar et al., Thalassiosira rotula / T. gravida reassessment

numbered_tempere_peragallo_objects.scientific_afterlife: Specimens were re-examined and figured in a 2025 study of Epithemia hyndmanii type material.
numbered_tempere_peragallo_objects.evidence_source: Kociolek et al. 2025, Epithemia hyndmanii study

moller_acquisition_and_extent.historical_acquisition_reading: A detailed Frenguelli biography states that he acquired part of J. D. Möller's Typenplatten and the Tempère & Peragallo 1907–1915 collection as reference material for his diatom research.

current_museum_team_2025.source: Guerrero, Delgadillo, Serino, Vouilloud & Lamaro, 'Colecciones de diatomeas adquiridas por J. Frenguelli para el Museo de La Plata', 2025 poster
current_museum_team_2025.interpretive_value: The Möller material is no longer merely a named legacy collection; current curatorial research gives a bounded surviving extent and acquisition-through-Frenguelli context.

frenguelli_bridge.biographical_source: Riccardi et al./UNLP historical study of Joaquín Frenguelli
facts: Frenguelli assembled his own large numbered diatom preparation collection.
He acquired a specialized diatom library including material from major British and European diatomists.
He acquired part of Möller's Typenplatten and the Tempère & Peragallo 1907–1915 collection.
His diatom preparations, reference collections, personal library, files and scientific papers were later retained in Museo de La Plata structures.
frenguelli_bridge.historical_mechanism: commercial/reference series -> private/professional acquisition by Frenguelli -> active comparative research material -> institutional retention at Museo de La Plata -> modern taxonomic reuse

archive_route.institution: Archivo Histórico del Museo de La Plata
archive_route.holdings: Incoming/outgoing museum correspondence from 1884–1970, administrative documentation, departmental records and Frenguelli manuscript collections.
archive_route.targeted_question: Locate purchase, invoice, dealer correspondence, donation or internal transfer records for Frenguelli's acquisition of Möller and Tempère & Peragallo material.
archive_route.upgrade_if_found: Would convert acquisition context into S transaction provenance.

series_history_guard.tempere_peragallo_first_edition: The first Diatomées Collection was issued 1889–1895 and is a nineteenth-century numbered material publication, but the current LPC object examples recovered in this pass are from the second edition / Tempère & Peragallo II, 1907–1915.
series_history_guard.claim_limit: Do not silently use surviving second-edition slides 51/64 as proof that a nineteenth-century first-edition set survives at La Plata.
series_history_guard.next_bounded_test: Ask the División Ficología for inventory fields distinguishing Tempère & Peragallo edition, series number and box/tray order; then identify any first-edition 1889–1895 slides separately.

comparison_with_cole.cole: Publication identity was materially stabilized by one 1–52 cabinet address system.
comparison_with_cole.tempere_peragallo: A numbered distributed diatom reference series preserved slide numbers as bibliographic/taxonomic addresses across institutions and continues to function as a reference/type resource.
comparison_with_cole.moller: Prepared diatom standards/reference sets entered later professional and museum collections as comparative tools, with maker/series identity surviving institutional re-addressing.
comparison_with_cole.payoff: La Plata supplies a different survival regime from Cole: serial numbers remain scientifically actionable even when the series is absorbed into a research collection rather than retained as one cabinet-volume.

exact_source_actions.upgrade_if_found: Closes series completeness and identifies any nineteenth-century first-edition survival.

exact_source_actions.upgrade_if_found: Closes transaction provenance at S level.

guards: The 122 Möller count comes from current museum-team research and should be retained as a dated collection state until an inventory export is obtained.
Do not equate a Tempère & Peragallo slide number with an LPC accession number; they are separate address namespaces.
Do not infer complete series survival from two securely documented numbered slides.
Do not collapse Frenguelli's own 2,435-preparation collection into the separately acquired Möller and Tempère & Peragallo reference sets.
